decision.reason: This adds AI assistance without replacing business ownership or audit state.
decision.reject: Reject automatic writes from unverified generated content.

workedTrace: A business record enters a document workflow.
A processing service extracts candidate fields.
Validation or human review accepts the fields.
The system of record receives only approved values.

failure.symptom: Generated data overwrites a business record without validation.
failure.check: Trace extraction, validation, approval, and write permissions.
failure.fix: Gate updates on schema checks and authorized approval.

experiment.change: Change the flow to add validation before the system write.
experiment.observe: Observe rejected fields, correction rate, and verified updates.
experiment.limit: Business value depends on workflow fit and input quality.

masteryQuestion: How should a GenAI workflow update a system of record?
masteryAnswer: Validate the generated fields and apply required approval before an authorized update.

title: Developer productivity tools
principle: Developer AI tools can assist code tasks, but generated changes still need engineering review.
mechanism: Use coding assistants for suggestions, explanation, tests, or refactoring within repository and security controls.

decision.when: Use this skill when GenAI can reduce development effort without weakening quality gates.
decision.choice: Apply suggestions through the normal code review and test process.
decision.reason: The developer retains responsibility for correctness and data handling.
decision.reject: Reject unreviewed generated code or secrets pasted into prompts.

workedTrace: A developer requests help with an API integration.
The assistant proposes a code change.
The developer reviews it against the SDK contract and repository rules.
CI and code review check behavior before merge.

failure.symptom: Generated code compiles but uses an unsupported API or broad permissions.
failure.check: Inspect service documentation, permissions, data handling, and tests.
failure.fix: Correct the implementation and preserve normal review gates.

experiment.change: Change the workflow to require security and contract review for generated code.
experiment.observe: Observe defect detection and developer time without skipping quality checks.
experiment.limit: Assistant output may be outdated, incomplete, or insecure.

masteryQuestion: What role should an AI code assistant play in a production workflow?
masteryAnswer: It can propose or explain code. Engineers and quality gates must verify and approve changes.

title: Advanced GenAI applications
principle: Advanced applications combine prompts, agents, and workflows to handle multi-step tasks.
mechanism: Choose orchestration patterns from task structure and side effects. Use reusable prompt chains or agents with explicit tools and stopping rules.

decision.when: Use this skill when a simple one-call interaction cannot meet the task requirement.
decision.choice: Compose explicit stages and contracts, using an agent only where dynamic tool choice helps.
decision.reason: Clear stages support validation and recovery.
decision.reject: Reject complexity that adds model calls without improving task outcome.

workedTrace: A document workflow needs extraction, policy comparison, and approval.
A workflow extracts structured facts and validates them.
A model compares facts with retrieved policy evidence.
A reviewer approves before a consequential system action.

failure.symptom: The agent makes an unsupported decision or loops through redundant calls.
failure.check: Inspect stage contracts, evidence, tool calls, and stop behavior.
failure.fix: Use deterministic steps for known work and guard model-selected branches.

experiment.change: Change the orchestration from a single prompt to explicit validated stages.
experiment.observe: Observe correctness, completion, calls, and side effects.
experiment.limit: More sophisticated architecture also increases failure and maintenance costs.

masteryQuestion: How should a team choose between workflow stages and agent decisions?
masteryAnswer: Use explicit workflow stages for known sequences and agent choice only where the path depends on context.

title: GenAI troubleshooting
principle: Troubleshooting improves when logs and traces show each request boundary and failure class.
mechanism: Use CloudWatch Logs Insights, X-Ray, request IDs, and model error details to inspect latency and failures.

decision.when: Use this skill when an FM application has unexplained errors, delay, or response regressions.
decision.choice: Trace the request from caller through retrieval, inference, tools, and response.
decision.reason: A boundary trace narrows root cause and avoids blind prompt changes.
decision.reject: Reject storing all sensitive prompts as the default diagnostic method.

workedTrace: A user reports a delayed answer.
The operator finds the trace ID and checks stage spans.
The trace shows repeated retrieval retries before inference.
The owner corrects retrieval behavior and confirms recovery.

failure.symptom: Teams change prompts even when the API or retrieval stage failed.
failure.check: Check request ID, error class, stage timing, model route, and source results.
failure.fix: Fix the first failing boundary and verify the full request path.

experiment.change: Change instrumentation to record stage duration and error class.
experiment.observe: Observe whether a test timeout can be localized without full prompt capture.
experiment.limit: Logs can contain sensitive data and require access and retention controls.

masteryQuestion: What should an operator inspect before editing a prompt for a failed answer?
masteryAnswer: Trace request stages, errors, route, and retrieval evidence to locate the first failed boundary.
